title: No Seat in JoSAA Round 1, Round 2, or the Final Round? Here's What Happens Next
description: Not getting a seat in an early JoSAA round is normal and doesn't remove you from counselling. A round-by-round walkthrough of what happens, what you must do, and what options remain after the final round.
author: Studyloaf Team

content.body: Seeing "not allotted" after JoSAA Round 1 is one of the most stressful moments of the whole JEE cycle, and one of the most misunderstood. Plenty of candidates get no seat in the first round and a seat in a later one, because closing ranks move as other students freeze, float, slide and withdraw. What decides the outcome is mostly whether you know what each round expects of you. This walkthrough follows the Joint Seat Allocation Authority's official FAQ and Business Rules for JoSAA 2026. The structure is stable from year to year, but rounds, dates and fees are revised annually, so check the current year's documents on the JoSAA portal before acting on anything here. For the bigger picture of how JoSAA and CSAB fit together, see our post on JoSAA vs CSAB.

content.heading: Before Round 1: the choice list you lock is the one used in every round
content.body: JoSAA allots seats using the ranked choice list you fill and lock during the choice-filling window. Once that window closes you can't reorder it or add new choices, and the same list is used in every round that follows. So the quality of your list decides most of what happens next. It should include every program you would genuinely be willing to join, in your real order of preference, with some realistic and safe options below your dream choices. A short list made up only of reach options is the most common reason a student goes through every round with nothing.

content.heading: If you get no seat in Round 1
content.body: Nothing is lost. A candidate with no allotment is automatically considered again in the next round, using the same locked choices. You don't need to pay anything, upload anything or click anything to stay in. All it means is that in Round 1 your rank didn't fall within the closing rank of any program on your list. Closing ranks usually rise in later rounds as seats are released by students who withdraw, fail document verification or get upgraded elsewhere. The one thing not to do is choose "Exit" in a panic. Under the JoSAA 2026 rules, exiting takes you out of all further JoSAA rounds.

content.heading: If you get a seat in Round 1 but want something better
content.body: This is where the most seats are lost by mistake. To keep any allotted seat, you must complete every step of online reporting within that round's deadline:

list: Choose Freeze (keep this seat and stop), Float (keep it, but take a higher choice at any institute if one opens up) or Slide (keep it, but take a higher choice within the same institute if one opens up). If the allotted seat is already your first choice, only Freeze is offered
Upload the required documents and respond to any queries raised during verification
Pay the Seat Acceptance Fee: ₹30,000, or ₹15,000 for SC, ST and PwD category tags, in JoSAA 2026. It includes ₹5,000 of non-refundable processing charges

If you miss any step, the seat is cancelled and you are out of all later JoSAA rounds. Not getting the seat you wanted is never a reason to skip reporting: accept it with Float or Slide and keep your place in the queue

content.heading: Rounds 2 to 4: still nothing, or still waiting for an upgrade
content.body: The same logic carries through the middle rounds. With no seat, you stay in automatically. With an accepted seat on Float or Slide, a higher choice in a later round replaces your current seat automatically, and you must complete online reporting again for the new one. If nothing better comes, you keep what you have. You can move from Float to Slide or Freeze, and from Slide to Freeze, in any round except the last. You can never move back from Freeze. Two exit routes matter here, and they are different. "Exit" is for a candidate who has no seat and wants out. "Withdraw" is for a candidate who holds a seat and wants out. Either one ends your JoSAA participation entirely, for IITs and NIT+ institutes alike. In 2026, withdrawing from an IIT or IISc seat was allowed only up to the round before the last.

content.heading: Planning to retake JEE Advanced? The withdrawal deadline matters
content.body: If you accept an IIT seat but decide to prepare for JEE Advanced again instead, the JoSAA 2026 FAQ says you must withdraw before the last round to stay eligible for the next year's JEE Advanced, provided you meet that year's other criteria. Withdrawal from an IIT seat is not possible in the final round itself. There is one exception: a candidate allotted an IIT seat for the first time in the final round who doesn't complete reporting remains eligible to appear in JEE Advanced the following year.

content.heading: The final round
content.body: JoSAA 2026 ran five rounds of seat allocation. In the final round, Float and Slide no longer do anything, because there is no later round to upgrade into. Whatever you are allotted, you either accept it or lose it. Candidates holding an NIT+ seat at the end of the final round also have to pay a Partial Admission Fee by the stated deadline. Not paying it counts as rejecting the seat, and once paid it is not refundable, though it is adjusted against the institute's admission fee. The FAQ is explicit that there is no spot round at any IIT or IISc after the final round. If you finish the last round with no IIT seat, that route is closed for the year.

content.heading: No seat after the final round: what's left
content.body: This is where most students give up too early. Several real options remain:

list: CSAB Special Rounds. After JoSAA ends, the Central Seat Allocation Board runs two special rounds to fill seats still vacant at NITs, IIEST, IIITs, SPAs and other NIT+ institutes. IITs do not take part. Candidates who got no JoSAA seat are explicitly eligible, as are candidates who exited, candidates whose seat was cancelled for non-payment, and eligible JEE Main rankers who never registered for JoSAA

CSAB needs a fresh registration on its own portal and a Special Round Enrolment Fee: ₹40,000 for GEN, GEN-EWS and OBC-NCL candidates and ₹19,000 for SC, ST and PwD candidates in 2026. Nothing carries over from JoSAA automatically, and a candidate who doesn't register in the CSAB window is not considered at all

State counselling. Several states fill seats in their own engineering colleges partly on JEE Main scores, through their own counselling process with its own registration and deadlines, which often overlap with JoSAA. Check your state's counselling authority while JoSAA is still running, not after it ends
Institutes with their own admissions. Many good private universities and some public institutes admit through their own entrance tests or merit lists, often on timelines that run alongside JoSAA
Taking a drop year. A real option for some students and the wrong one for others. Our post on whether to drop a year for JEE or NEET covers how to decide honestly

content.heading: Common mistakes
list: Choosing Exit after Round 1 because nothing was allotted. You were going to be considered in Round 2 anyway
Skipping the Seat Acceptance Fee or document upload because the allotted seat wasn't your favourite. That cancels the seat and removes you from every later round
Picking Freeze out of nervousness when you actually wanted a better option. Freeze can't be undone
Assuming CSAB registration happens automatically for JoSAA candidates. It doesn't, and there is a separate fee
Missing the IIT withdrawal deadline when planning to retake JEE Advanced
Ignoring queries raised on your uploaded documents. Unanswered queries can lead to cancellation even after you've paid

content.heading: A calm way to get through it
content.body: Write every JoSAA and CSAB deadline into one list the day the schedule is published, and check the portal after every round result even when you expect nothing to have changed. Most of the damage in counselling comes from missed steps, not bad ranks. And if counselling doesn't go your way this year and you decide to try again, Studyloaf's free timetable generator can turn a fresh year of prep into a weekly plan in a couple of minutes, without needing an account.
